rationale: The run produced results/bivariate_irfs.json with suppress_feedback = {employment_plateau_with_feedback: -0.011717, employment_plateau_without_feedback: -0.014579}, and the emp_wage IRF at year 0 gives the initial employment change of -0.01 (the -1% shock). Expressing plateaus as multiples of the initial change: with wage feedback -0.011717/-0.01 = 1.17x (paper 1.2, 2.4% relative error -> match) and without wage feedback -0.014579/-0.01 = 1.46x (paper 1.6, 8.9% relative error -> outside the 5% band but well within 30%). Both values reproduce the paper's qualitative finding that suppressing wage feedback raises the long-run employment response only modestly, but the without-feedback value falls in the partial (>5%, <30%) band, so the combined scalar claim is graded partial. The figure figures/fig14_suppress_feedback.png corresponds to this output.
